Select and Record the Modeling Cohort From Raw Event Data

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
profile_select_cohort.Rd

Stage 0 of the resistance-profiling pipeline. Every eligibility, precision, and panel-feasibility calculation downstream of this function must be computed on the SAME cohort that will eventually be fit – never on the full dataset while fitting only a restricted subset (e.g. discharged-only events). This function makes that restriction an explicit, traceable step instead of an assumption buried in a script.

Usage

profile_select_cohort(data, filters, event_id_col = NULL)

Arguments

data

Data frame of events/isolates.

filters

Named list. Each name is a column in data; each value is a character/numeric vector of values that column must match (via %in%) for a row to survive. Applied in list order (e.g. list(final_outcome = "Discharged", center_name = my_hospitals)).

event_id_col

Character or NULL. Reserved for future event-level manifest detail; currently unused beyond validating it is present if supplied.

Value

A list:

data

the filtered data frame

manifest

one row per filter applied, in order: column, values (comma-joined), n_before, n_after, n_excluded

Details

Filters are applied in the order supplied, each an exact-match inclusion rule against one column. The returned manifest shows how many rows survived EACH filter in sequence, so a caller can see exactly how much a given restriction removed on its own, rather than only one before/after total that hides which criterion did the work.

This filters rows; it does not attach a clinical label to the result. Restricting to final_outcome == "Discharged" describes exactly that cohort, not automatically "all non-fatal infections" – transfers, ongoing admissions, or other surviving-but-not-discharged outcomes are excluded by that specific restriction, and the caller should label the resulting cohort accordingly rather than assuming the broader label.
